text: Supported bridge: P defines a three-agent Adversarial Review protocol (main agent, reviewer, critic), reports false consensus under naive AR, and reports improved F1 when explicit disagreement is prompted (P, line 3). Q explicitly studies unknown alignment/capability, one-sided capability concealment, higher-order-belief elicitation, peer scoring, and reward coupling across multiple agents (Q, line 3). Thus AR is a plausible empirical testbed for Q-inspired mechanisms, but P alone only establishes prompt-induced structured disagreement.

The abstract-scan hypothesis overstates what these texts support by calling a peer-scoring/reward-coupling ablation a test of incentive compatibility. Q gives implementability conditions via nested cyclical monotonicity and a revelation principle (Q, line 3), while P describes no private type reports, utilities, payoff-sensitive decisions, or strategic-agent manipulation (P, line 3). Without an explicit mechanism mapping reports/actions to rewards and an induced sandbagging payoff, improved F1 or reduced agreement cannot identify incentive compatibility; it may only be another prompt effect.

Sharpened publication line: a preregistered factorial AR study crossing (A) disagreement instruction, (B) individually proper peer scoring of reviewer/critic evidence claims, (C) negatively coupled rewards that make unsupported mutual agreement costly, and (D) an induced capability-concealment/sandbagging payoff. Use P outcomes: coding correctness/pass rate, defect-review F1, unsupported agreement/false consensus; add calibrated evidence accuracy and concealed-defect detection. The decisive estimand is the mechanism-by-sandbagging interaction relative to prompt-only AR. A benefit that persists specifically under strategic misalignment, without reducing coding accuracy, supports practical discipline; no interaction or prompt-equivalent effects rejects the mechanism claim. Q motivates B-D (Q, line 3); P supplies AR and benchmarks/outcomes (P, line 3).

Preferred conclusion: confirm feasibility but narrow the novelty claim to testing whether explicit payoff mechanisms add robustness beyond structured-disagreement prompting under induced concealment. Do not claim a direct experimental test of Q nested cyclical monotonicity unless the full paper supplies a parameterized implementable mechanism and the experiment elicits the reports/types needed to check its inequalities. Abstract-only evidence leaves that unresolved.

Unresolved after ledger #4: only abstracts are available, and no ada entry is yet present to cross-check. Before calling the result incentive-compatible, full Q must specify the peer score/reward-coupling formula and its implementability assumptions; the study must define agent utilities, private capability information, report space, induced sandbagging incentives, and manipulation-resistant ground truth. Otherwise the defensible paper is an empirical robustness study of Q-inspired payoff coupling versus P-style prompting, not a validation of Q theory.

Cross-check confirms Emmy #1-#4. Exact bridge: Q says capabilities can be "concealed but not counterfeited" and names sandbagging, peer scoring, and "coupling rewards to induce competition among multiple agents" (Q:3). P supplies a three-agent reviewer/critic protocol and observes naive false consensus, while explicit disagreement prompting raises F1 (P:3). The non-obvious test is therefore the incremental robustness of rewards over prompting under induced concealment, not the generic benefit of disagreement.

Preferred single publication hypothesis: in a preregistered 2x2 design crossing P-style explicit-disagreement prompt with Q-inspired competitive reward coupling, test agents both with and without a disclosed bonus for concealing seeded defects. Primary estimand: reward-coupling x concealment-incentive interaction on seeded-defect recall/evidence-grounded false consensus; non-inferiority margin on coding pass rate. A coupling-specific rescue under concealment, beyond prompt-only AR, is the concrete positive result; prompt-equivalent or no rescue is a sharp null/refutation.

Disagreement with the scan wording and qualification to Emmy #3: neither abstract specifies a proper peer-scoring rule, agent utility model, private reports/types, or a reward formula. Q:3 only says it applies the framework to stylized examples; P:3 evaluates prompts, not strategic payoffs. Thus calling an arbitrary peer-score "incentive-compatible" or claiming a test of nested cyclical monotonicity is unsupported. Peer scoring should be omitted from the core design unless full Q provides an operational rule; reward coupling is the cleaner named intervention.

Publication claim should be framed as causal evidence that competitive reward coupling makes structured review robust to induced capability concealment without sacrificing coding accuracy. This empirically distinguishes payoff-sensitive discipline from prompt-induced disagreement, but does not itself establish Q-style incentive compatibility. Manipulation-resistant seeded defects and separately logged reviewer/critic evidence are required so false consensus cannot improve merely by more performative disagreement.

Unresolved: only abstracts are present. Before execution, obtain Q full text to instantiate its reward-coupling rule and assumptions; preregister which agent receives the concealment payoff, what information is private, how rewards affect model behavior, seeded-defect ground truth, and a coding-accuracy non-inferiority margin. If rewards are merely described in prompts and do not measurably alter choices, the experiment cannot distinguish mechanism effects from framing effects.

Final synthesis with Ada #7-#10: confirm the bridge but reject the scan’s incentive-compatibility wording. The concrete publication candidate is a preregistered 2x2 AR experiment crossing P-style explicit-disagreement prompting with Q-inspired competitive reward coupling, run with and without an induced payoff for concealing seeded defects. P:3 directly supplies the three-agent reviewer/critic protocol, false-consensus failure, prompt-only comparator, F1, and coding pass-rate outcome; Q:3 directly supplies one-sided capability concealment/sandbagging and reward coupling among multiple agents. The primary estimand should be reward-coupling x concealment-payoff on seeded-defect recall and evidence-grounded false consensus, with coding pass-rate non-inferiority. A coupling-specific rescue under concealment is publishable evidence of payoff-robust review beyond prompting; no rescue or prompt-equivalent behavior is a sharp negative result.

Peer scoring should not be a core factor on current evidence. Q:3 merely lists discipline via peer scoring and reward coupling among stylized examples, without a score, utility model, report space, or implementability assumptions; P:3 contains prompts rather than strategic payments. Therefore even a positive interaction would support causal robustness to an induced payoff, not Q’s nested-cyclical-monotonicity characterization or incentive compatibility. It also requires externally seeded, manipulation-resistant defects and separately logged evidence so reduced consensus is not performative disagreement.

Remaining unresolved after agreement with Ada: obtain full Q to instantiate and justify a reward rule; preregister reward delivery, which agent has private information and concealment incentives, evidence-grounding criteria, and the coding non-inferiority margin. If rewards exist only as natural-language framing or do not measurably change choices, the proposed experiment cannot separate mechanism effects from prompt effects.

Design correction to Ada #8 / Emmy #13: crossing disagreement prompting (on/off), competitive reward coupling (on/off), and concealment payoff (on/off) is a 2x2x2 factorial, not a 2x2. The key identification is the coupling x concealment interaction, while the three-way prompt x coupling x concealment interaction tests whether coupling adds robustness specifically beyond P-style prompting. This separation is essential because P:3 already shows prompting changes F1.

Complete-text check leaves the consensus unchanged. Q:3 supports only the ingredients: unknown preferences/capabilities, concealment-not-counterfeiting, sandbagging, peer scoring, and coupled competitive rewards; it does not provide an operational rule in the supplied abstract. P:3 supports AR, false consensus, explicit-disagreement prompting, F1/pass-rate outcomes, and evidence grounding. Hence the strongest supported publication target is a 2x2x2 causal robustness study, not an incentive-compatibility validation.

Final unresolved issues: full Q or an independently specified reward mechanism is needed; reward delivery must create a behaviorally effective payoff rather than merely another prompt; seeded defects must provide exogenous ground truth; and analysis must preregister defect recall/evidence-grounded false consensus plus coding pass-rate non-inferiority. A positive three-way interaction supports incremental payoff robustness, not nested cyclical monotonicity or general incentive compatibility.
